responses.content:
The statement is incorrect. Penicillin was not discovered by Louis Pasteur.

Penicillin was actually discovered by Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming in 1928, not 1921. Fleming observed that a mold (Penicillium notatum) had contaminated one of his bacterial cultures and that the mold had killed off the surrounding bacteria.

Fleming's discovery led to the development of penicillin as a medicine, which was first isolated and purified by Howard Florey and Ernst Boris Chain in the early 1940s. They conducted further research on the antibiotic and worked with the pharmaceutical company Pfizer to develop it into a treatment for bacterial infections.

Louis Pasteur (1822-1895) was a French scientist who made significant contributions to vaccination, germ theory, and the development of pasteurization, but he did not discover penicillin.
